data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for planning and managing USDA’s wireless networks and devices that use USDA wireless networks.
policy_statements.target: USDA’s wireless networks and devices that use USDA wireless networks

policy_statements.source_text: This DR replaces Departmental Manual (DM) 3300-005, Policies for Planning and Managing Wireless Technologies in USDA, dated November 10, 2010.
policy_statements.target: Departmental Manual (DM) 3300-005, Policies for Planning and Managing Wireless Technologies in USDA
cross_references: Departmental Manual (DM) 3300-005, Policies for Planning and Managing Wireless Technologies in USDA

policy_statements.source_text: This DR will be in effect until superseded or the expiration date.
conditions: until superseded or the expiration date

policy_statements.source_text: The term “wireless network” encompasses any network that uses the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Standards Association (IEEE-SA) 802.11 Standards, such as Wireless Local Area Networks (WLAN) or Wireless Fidelity (Wi-Fi).
cross_references: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Standards Association (IEEE-SA) 802.11 Standards

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will align their policies and procedures with this DR within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices may supplement this DR when developing their internal guidance.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: when developing their internal guidance

policy_statements.source_text: Modifications to the intent or purpose of this DR are not allowed.
policy_statements.target: Modifications to the intent or purpose of this DR

policy_statements.source_text: If Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices publish internal guidance that supplements this DR, one copy of each supplement will be forwarded to the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), Digital Infrastructure Services Center (DISC), Enterprise Network Services (ENS), Telecommunications Infrastructure Management and Governance (TIMG) at ens.policy@usda.gov.
conditions: If Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices publish internal guidance that supplements this DR

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to USDA wireless networks and devices (e.g., laptops) that use USDA wireless networks.
policy_statements.target: USDA wireless networks and devices (e.g., laptops) that use USDA wireless networks

policy_statements.source_text: This DR excludes wireless devices (e.g., cellular phones) that are provisioned for use on a third-party cellular network.
policy_statements.target: wireless devices (e.g., cellular phones) that are provisioned for use on a third-party cellular network

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, contractors, data centers, cooperative partners, and others working for, or on behalf of, the USDA.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, contractors, data centers, cooperative partners, and others working for, or on behalf of, the USDA

policy_statements.source_text: The widespread adoption of wireless technologies within USDA represents a paradigm shift from telecommunications landline technologies.

This shift introduces management challenges due to the pervasive availability of wireless consumer products in the marketplace and the tendency for USDA to treat wireless acquisitions as commodity buys.

The most significant business challenges associated with a commodity approach to buying wireless technologies occur when the lack of a central acquisition strategy results in fractionalized purchases of non-standard products and services.
As this practice continues, the Department loses visibility and control of wireless technologies.
Thus, a policy is needed to ensure that there is a more strategic, centralized management of wireless technologies.

Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are required to receive approval from the USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) prior to the purchase of any wireless networking technologies regardless of the dollar amount.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: prior to the purchase of any wireless networking technologies regardless of the dollar amount

policy_statements.source_text: These purchases include all software and equipment for the implementation of new wireless networks as well as upgrades or changes to existing wireless networks.
policy_statements.target: all software and equipment for the implementation of new wireless networks as well as upgrades or changes to existing wireless networks

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area, agency, and staff office approval requests for wireless networks will describe business and security requirements, include a cost trade-off analysis between the proposed wireless network and a hardwired network with equivalent capabilities, and provide total anticipated costs for each.

Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are required to submit an annual report to the USDA OCIO telecommunications management staff that accounts for all wireless networks and associated infrastructure, and ensure that the information provided is mapped into the agency or staff office enterprise architecture (EA).
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: annual report to the USDA OCIO telecommunications management staff that accounts for all wireless networks and associated infrastructure

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area, agencies, and staff offices will ensure technical personnel are adequately trained to oversee the planning, development, implementation, and management of wireless networks in order to be compliant with the USDA Quality of Service (QoS)/Class of Service (CoS) Standard (eAuthentication access required).
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agencies, and staff offices
cross_references: USDA Quality of Service (QoS)/Class of Service (CoS) Standard

policy_statements.source_text: All Internet Protocol (IP) based data transmission (e.g., email) to and from Government networks will be registered with USDA Domain Name System (DNS) servers and routed through the USDA secure internet gateways.
policy_statements.target: Internet Protocol (IP) based data transmission (e.g., email) to and from Government networks

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies and staff offices will establish continuous access monitoring and reporting capabilities that identify the media access control (MAC) address for authorized users and can be referenced to the specific wireless device and to the user’s profile.
policy_statements.target: continuous access monitoring and reporting capabilities that identify the media access control (MAC) address for authorized users and can be referenced to the specific wireless device and to the user’s profile

policy_statements.source_text: Wireless usage reports will be analyzed by Mission Area, agency, or staff office telecommunications subject matter experts (SME) to:
Ensure that networks are secure and engineered in a manner that maintains high QoS to USDA customers;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office telecommunications subject matter experts (SME)

policy_statements.source_text: Identify usage trends to improve future acquisition decisions; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office telecommunications subject matter experts (SME)

policy_statements.source_text: Determine corrective actions that address excessive, infrequent, or non-usage of Government-issued devices.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office telecommunications subject matter experts (SME)
policy_statements.target: corrective actions that address excessive, infrequent, or non-usage of Government-issued devices

policy_statements.source_text: USDA OCIO will establish enterprise contracts or place task orders through General Services Administration (GSA) contracts for wireless technologies.
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will limit wireless device purchases to those technologies that are available through GSA contracts approved by the USDA CIO.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: those technologies that are available through GSA contracts approved by the USDA CIO

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will appoint Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officers (TMACO) to place orders for all wireless technologies.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: USDA OCIO will facilitate the Departmental adoption of next generation wireless technologies and eliminate redundant Mission Area, agency, or staff office pilot tests of wireless networks.
policy_statements.target: Departmental adoption of next generation wireless technologies

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will follow OCIO procedures for conducting and coordinating pilot tests and share test results with each other through the OCIO established processes.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: OCIO procedures for conducting and coordinating pilot tests

policy_statements.source_text: USDA wireless networks and devices may be used for, but are not limited to, the following purposes:
The communication and exchange of data between State and local governments, private sector organizations, and educational and research institutions, both in the United States and abroad;
The development of internet-based projects;
Interactive sharing of information without compromising USDA secured data;
The exchange of any non-sensitive data between USDA entities in support of Mission Area, agency, and staff office missions, or other official purposes; and
The distribution and collection of information related to official program delivery that is in compliance with Federal and Departmental guidelines.

In accordance with the Federal CIO Council’s Recommended Executive Branch Model Policy/Guidance on "Limited Personal Use" of Government Office Equipment Including Information Technology (Limited Personal Use), May 19, 1999, employees may use Government wireless devices for personal matters on an occasional basis provided that there is no loss of employee productivity or interference with official employee duties.
conditions: on an occasional basis
provided that there is no loss of employee productivity or interference with official employee duties
cross_references: Federal CIO Council’s Recommended Executive Branch Model Policy/Guidance on "Limited Personal Use" of Government Office Equipment Including Information Technology (Limited Personal Use), May 19, 1999

policy_statements.source_text: In accordance with the Limited Personal Use guidance, employees will not use USDA wireless networks and devices:
To conduct illegal, inappropriate, or offensive activities to fellow employees or the public.
Such activities include, but are not limited to, hate speech or material that ridicules others on the basis of race, creed, religion, color, sex, disability, or national origin;
To create, download, view, store, copy, or transmit sexually explicit or sexually oriented materials;
To create, download, view, store, copy, or transmit materials related to illegal gambling, illegal weapons, terrorist activities, and any other illegal activities or activities otherwise prohibited;
To conduct activities that could cause congestion, delay, or disruption of service to any Government system or equipment.
For example, greeting cards, video, or other large file attachments can degrade the performance of the entire network;
For commercial purposes or in support of “for-profit” activities or other outside employment or business activity (e.g., consulting for pay or sales of goods and services);
To engage in any outside fundraising activity, endorse any product or service, participate in any lobbying activity, or engage in any prohibited partisan political activity;
To post Departmental information to external newsgroups, bulletin boards, or other public forums without authority; and
To conduct activities that could generate more than a minimal expense to the Government.

In accordance with the Limited Personal Use, it is the responsibility of employees to ensure they are not giving the false impression that they are acting in an official capacity when they are using Government office equipment for non-Government purposes.
conditions: when they are using Government office equipment for non-Government purposes

policy_statements.source_text: If there is an expectation that such a personal use could be interpreted to represent a Mission Area, agency, or staff office, then an adequate disclaimer must be used.
conditions: If there is an expectation that such a personal use could be interpreted to represent a Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: One acceptable disclaimer is “The contents of this message are mine personally and do not reflect any position of the Government or my agency.”

It is the responsibility of employees not to use or wear any official Government logos, trademarks, seals, or insignias while displaying, portraying, or posting any acts that would be detrimental to the Government, including any State, local, or federally illegal activities, or any of the previously mentioned prohibited activities.
policy_statements.target: any official Government logos, trademarks, seals, or insignias
conditions: while displaying, portraying, or posting any acts that would be detrimental to the Government, including any State, local, or federally illegal activities, or any of the previously mentioned prohibited activities

policy_statements.source_text: USDA employees will use Government wireless networks and devices with the understanding that such use serves as consent to monitoring of any type of use, including incidental and personal uses, whether authorized or unauthorized.
In addition, access of such systems is not anonymous.
For example, for each use of the internet over Government systems, these systems may capture information transmitted, received, or stored on the system.
policy_statements.target: information transmitted, received, or stored on the system
conditions: for each use of the internet over Government systems

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA CIO will:
Provide leadership to Mission Area, agency, and staff office programs for the integration of wireless technologies into the existing USDA infrastructure;
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office programs

policy_statements.source_text: Set the priorities for USDA wireless programs, projects, and activities based on Departmentwide business requirements and available resources;
policy_statements.target: priorities for USDA wireless programs, projects, and activities
conditions: based on Departmentwide business requirements and available resources

policy_statements.source_text: Obtain the financial and human resources to implement USDA wireless programs, projects, and activities;
Represent the USDA to oversight agencies on wireless technologies-related issues;
Serve as the USDA representative to the Diplomatic Telecommunications Service Program Office (DTSPO);

Respond to oversight agencies, such as Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Government Accountability Office (GAO), Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Department of Commerce (DOC), and Federal Communications Commission (FCC), with timely and accurate USDA telecommunications program and cost information; and
Perform management and oversight responsibilities in accordance with the Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291, as applicable to this directive.
cross_references: Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291
conditions: as applicable to this directive

policy_statements.source_text: The ENS Director will:
Establish policies and procedures for the management of wireless technologies throughout USDA;
policy_statements.target: policies and procedures for the management of wireless technologies throughout USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Oversee Mission Area, agency, and staff office compliance with USDA wireless technologies policies and procedures;
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office compliance with USDA wireless technologies policies and procedures

policy_statements.source_text: Manage USDA wireless technologies in accordance with prescribed laws, regulations, standards, and related USDA 3300 Series telecommunications directives;
Grant technical approval for acquisition of new wireless technologies when the analysis of the request indicates that this is the best approach for USDA;
conditions: when the analysis of the request indicates that this is the best approach for USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Review and render a decision for Mission Area, agency, and staff office policy waiver requests;
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office policy waiver requests

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain an electronic file of approved waivers;
Work with Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices to eliminate redundant or unused wireless technologies;
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Include wireless technology requirements and initiatives as part of the telecommunications planning process;
Use GSA and USDA mandated programs when Mission Area, agency, and staff office requirements can be met cost effectively; and
conditions: when Mission Area, agency, and staff office requirements can be met cost effectively

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain inventories of USDA wireless networks and devices to the extent necessary to:
Ensure that there are adequate and appropriate wireless networks and devices to support the Mission Area, agency, and staff office mission;
policy_statements.target: adequate and appropriate wireless networks and devices

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure accountability for USDA wireless networks and devices; and
Meet Departmental and Federal requests for periodic or special inventory reports.
policy_statements.target: Departmental and Federal requests for periodic or special inventory reports

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors will:
Ensure Mission Area, agency. and staff office personnel comply with this directive;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency. and staff office personnel

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure Mission Area, agency, and staff office internal directives conform to this DR’s stated requirements;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office internal directives

policy_statements.source_text: Lead the cost-effective implementation of programmatic applications of wireless technologies;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
policy_statements.target: cost-effective implementation of programmatic applications of wireless technologies

policy_statements.source_text: Establish cooperative or collaborative programs with other Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices to promote the cost-effective adoption of wireless technologies throughout USDA;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
policy_statements.target: cooperative or collaborative programs with other Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Set priority levels for internal programs, projects, and activities, that include wireless technologies, basing these priorities on business requirements and available resources;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
policy_statements.target: priority levels for internal programs, projects, and activities, that include wireless technologies
conditions: basing these priorities on business requirements and available resources

policy_statements.source_text: Adhere to Federal and USDA wireless strategies, policies, standards, and best practices;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
policy_statements.target: Federal and USDA wireless strategies, policies, standards, and best practices

policy_statements.source_text: Align wireless technology planning, acquisition, design, integration, and management plans with the current USDA Information Technology Strategic Plan, USDA EA, USDA standards and Departmental directives, and Federal guidelines promulgated by Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP), OMB, National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA), Federal CIO Council, DHS, National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), FCC, and other Federal organizations that manage wireless technologies;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
policy_statements.target: wireless technology planning, acquisition, design, integration, and management plans

The widespread adoption of wireless technologies within USDA represents a paradigm shift from telecommunications landline technologies.

This shift introduces management challenges due to the pervasive availability of wireless consumer products in the marketplace and the tendency for USDA to treat wireless acquisitions as commodity buys.

The most significant business challenges associated with a commodity approach to buying wireless technologies occur when the lack of a central acquisition strategy results in fractionalized purchases of non-standard products and services.
As this practice continues, the Department loses visibility and control of wireless technologies.
Thus, a policy is needed to ensure that there is a more strategic, centralized management of wireless technologies.

Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are required to receive approval from the USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) prior to the purchase of any wireless networking technologies regardless of the dollar amount.

(2) In accordance with the Federal CIO Council’s  *Recommended Executive Branch Model Policy/Guidance on "Limited Personal Use" of Government Office Equipment Including Information Technology*  (*Limited Personal Use*), May 19, 1999, employees may use Government wireless devices for personal matters on an occasional basis provided that there is no loss of employee productivity or interference with official employee duties.
provided that there is no loss of employee productivity or interference with official employee duties
In accordance with the *Limited Personal Use* guidance, employees will not use USDA wireless networks and devices
To create, download, view, store, copy, or transmit materials related to illegal gambling, illegal weapons, terrorist activities, and any other illegal activities or activities otherwise prohibited;
To conduct activities that could cause congestion, delay, or disruption of service to any Government system or equipment.
For example, greeting cards, video, or other large file attachments can degrade the performance of the entire network;
For commercial purposes or in support of “for-profit” activities or other outside employment or business activity (e.g., consulting for pay or sales of goods and services);
To engage in any outside fundraising activity, endorse any product or service, participate in any lobbying activity, or engage in any prohibited partisan political activity;
To post Departmental information to external newsgroups, bulletin boards, or other public forums without authority; and
To conduct activities that could generate more than a minimal expense to the Government.
